author: reek
body: Sound is its own authority, and asking for it does not buy the machine.

author: reek
body: This opening declares [Audio] and nothing else of that family, then reads its own capability word back out of the process table. The bits it reports are the granted ones -- process-get-cap is what the kernel itself tests before it services a syscall -- not a restatement of the row above.

author: reek
body: The zeroes are the test. audio=1 alone would pass just as well on the old arrangement, where HdaAudio published [Device.Mmio] and a program that wanted to beep declared the Device family to get it: it would have earned the audio bit if one had existed, and the device and block bits with it. An attenuation is only visible in what it DENIES, so a pin that reports only what was granted cannot see this change at all.

author: reek
body: Microphone is reported too, and it must be 0. Speaking and listening are separate authorities over one controller, and the easy mistake -- giving the whole codec one bit -- would make the right to beep the right to hear the room. That is the more dangerous half, and nothing in the granted word would say so.
